components.css: .ds-specs { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 6px; width: 240px; margin: 0; } .ds-specs > div { background: var(--of-bg-elevated, #0f2238); border-radius: 6px; padding: 5px 8px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; } .ds-specs dt { font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--of-text-3, #84aabd); } .ds-specs dd { margin: 0; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--of-text-bright, #e0eaf8); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

narrative.overview:
OpenFishing is a tackle box: dark, ordered compartments where every lure has its numbered slot and its record. The world is the water at dusk. Deep, cool surfaces step up in small tonal increments, and a single accent glints against them like a lure catching the last light. Nothing is decorative for its own sake. Photos of real lures and catches carry the color, and the interface around them stays quiet and in order.

The system is an Operate surface first: people log catches one-handed on a phone at the bank, then sort and review their collection at home. Density is moderate. Cards and forms are compact, but the lure number, the name and the primary action are always the strongest things on screen. Every theme (Ocean, Forrest, Sunset, Dusk) is the same tackle box under a different light. The structure, spacing and type never change; only the semantic color set does, in both dark and light mode.

Direction: catalogued, built for outdoors. The confirmed target for new and reworked screens combines two moods. Precise, catalogued: the lure is an inventory item with a numbered plate and a spec sheet in tabular mono. Outdoorsy, practical: everything that matters survives a phone held in direct sun or used in the dark.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, tonal layering; light mode is a fully designed counterpart, not an inversion.
One accent per theme, used for actions, active state and the lure number, never as decoration.
DM Sans for everything readable; JetBrains Mono only for numbers that are catalogued (lure numbers, specs, measurements).
Flat surfaces with 1px borders; shadows appear only on floating layers.
Gently curved, consistent corners (9px controls, 14px cards).
Built to be readable at the water: the glare test is a design requirement.

rules.name: The Single Glint Rule
rules.body: Each theme has exactly one accent hue. It marks what you can act on and what is selected, and nothing else. Semantic colors are not accents and are never used for decoration.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Components take every color from --of-* semantic tokens, never from literals. A literal hex in a component breaks the other three themes and light mode. (The lure-number badge's photo scrim, rgba(0,0,0,0.62), is the one deliberate exception: it must be dark on every photo.)

rules.name: The Glare Rule (direction)
rules.body: On screens used at the water (lure cards, catch and spot forms, spot detail), information a person needs to read uses --of-text-2 or brighter. --of-text-4 is for hints and inactive states only, never for values.

rules.name: The Stencil Rule
rules.body: Mono type is reserved for catalogued numbers: lure numbers, weights, sizes, depths, counts, coordinates. Never for prose, labels or headings. Any column of digits uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (.of-num).

rules.name: The Long-Word Rule
rules.body: Every label must survive German and Polish string lengths: allow wrapping in buttons and chips, and never set a fixed width on text-bearing controls.

rules.name: The Thumb Rule (direction)
rules.body: On mobile, every tappable control on a field-use screen is at least 40px tall, and a form's primary action is full width and at least 48px.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards and panels never carry a shadow at rest. A shadow means "this is floating" (menu, toast, modal) or "you are pointing at this" (card hover glow).

dos: Do take every color from an --of-* token so all four themes and both modes work automatically.
Do check every new screen in dark and light mode, and in at least one non-Ocean theme.
Do keep one solid-accent primary action per view.
Do use JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals for lure numbers, measurements and counts, and nowhere else.
Do keep cards flat at rest (14px radius, 1px subtle border) and reserve shadows for floating layers.
Do run the glare test on field-use screens: secondary info at --of-text-2 or brighter, controls at least 40px, primary action at least 48px on mobile.
Do keep the wordmark and mark SVGs as they are, colored by currentColor from the theme accent.
donts: Don't use --of-text-4 for anything a person needs to read at the water; it is for hints and inactive states.
Don't introduce a second accent hue within a theme, or use semantic red/green/amber decoratively.
Don't add shadows to resting cards or panels.
Don't let filter bars or chip rows scroll horizontally; they wrap.
Don't give text-bearing controls fixed widths; nine languages have to fit.
Don't hardcode hex values in components, even for one theme.
